hero.headline: House GOP report faults Justice Department for decades of failures in Epstein case, urges reinterviewing witnesses
hero.body:
The House Oversight Committee released a Republican-led report Tuesday criticizing the Justice Department for its handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation over multiple decades and administrations, calling for federal investigators to reinterview key witnesses and associates of the late sex offender. The 137-page report stated that too many survivors and witnesses were never approached or properly questioned by federal authorities and urged the DOJ to interview or reinterview individuals who were part of the inner circle of Epstein and co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell.

Committee Chair James Comer said Epstein operated with impunity, shielded by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims. The report called for the Justice Department to investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity and ensure survivors have access to their records. The Justice Department responded that the Attorney General has repeatedly said the Epstein case is not closed and that there is no statute of limitations on human trafficking, adding that the department will continue following all additional investigative leads.

The report also questioned whether the Justice Department has released all relevant documents under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which mandated public disclosure of case-related records. The Republican report criticized the department for releasing names of some victims in documents while redacting the names of Epstein allies, and noted that survivors continue to ask the DOJ for access to their own personal files but have not been permitted to do so. The report called for legislation protecting the ability of individuals with knowledge of sexual abuse to speak freely regardless of nondisclosure agreements.

The top Democrat on the committee, Robert Garcia, said the Republican investigation was incomplete and that Democrats will hold public hearings when they take the majority in January. Garcia said the DOJ continues to illegally withhold over 2.5 million pages of documents. Democrats released their own report last month calling for an independent special counsel to investigate Epstein's ties to President Donald Trump, allegations the White House called untrue and politically motivated. The Republican report criticized Democrats for focusing on Trump, saying they were obsessed with the president and had engaged in an unfounded witch hunt.

cards.headline: Nvidia hires outside law firm for independent investigation into CEO's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
cards.body:
Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation into Chief Executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The company announced Tuesday that attorney Joon Kim, a former U.S. Attorney for New York's Southern District, will lead the probe. The FBI is conducting a separate investigation. Nvidia's share price has fallen nearly to a yearly low, with $500 billion wiped from its market value since Friday.

Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside his marriage with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer. According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top Washington officials in spring warning that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Beijing has denied the allegations, calling them intended to smear China. President Donald Trump said Monday he spoke with Jensen Huang, who told him he had no idea she was a spy, and that Trump believed him.

Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed-door briefing. A person familiar with the committee's demand said the Nvidia chief has not yet indicated whether he will attend. The committee has authority to subpoena him if deemed necessary.

Nvidia's board said Sunday it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised, and a committee of independent directors will oversee the investigation. Nvidia is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for operating AI tools and is the world's second most valuable company after Apple. Its chips have become a national security matter for U.S. officials seeking to win the AI race.

cards.headline: NRC grants X-energy construction permit for four small modular reactors at Texas Dow plant
cards.body:
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has approved a construction permit for X-energy to build four small modular reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas, the nuclear startup announced Monday. The permit marks the first approval for an advanced nuclear reactor at an industrial site in the United States. Each of the four Xe-100 reactors will be capable of generating 80 megawatts of electricity and 200 megawatts of heat, though the reactors are not expected to be operational until the early 2030s.

The nuclear industry has positioned small modular reactors as a faster and cheaper alternative to traditional nuclear plants, though those advantages remain unproven. No small modular reactor currently operates in the United States. X-energy says its design flows helium gas over uranium-containing fuel pellets, which the company claims is safer than many existing reactors.

Safety advocates criticized the approval process. Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety for the Union of Concerned Scientists, said in a statement that the NRC achieved the approval "by pushing consideration of critical safety questions to a later date—issues the NRC should've fully resolved before green lighting construction."

X-energy has attracted significant backing from technology companies seeking electricity sources for data centers. Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund led the company's $500 million Series C-1 funding round, and Amazon has committed to buying 5 gigawatts of capacity from the startup. X-energy raised $1 billion in an April initial public offering, but investor enthusiasm has cooled. The company's shares are trading at less than half their initial offering price.

cards.headline: Grok Build coding agent exposes thousands of users' confidential data through shareable links
cards.teaser: Security researchers find design flaw allows enumeration of live projects, revealing business plans, medical records, and SpaceXSI's own internal sales documents.
cards.body:
Security firm Claroc has found that Grok Build, a coding agent from SpaceXSI, is exposing confidential data from thousands of users through a design flaw in its shareable link system. Though the platform randomizes URLs, a developer decision allows anyone to enumerate live projects and access associated data, including business plans, medical exam results, and employee information.

Among the exposed material were documents from two dozen apps built by SpaceXSI itself, including a confidential onboarding plan for an enterprise sales team member, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, and advertising proposals. SpaceXSI began removing its own exposed links hours after receiving media inquiries, though most other users' data remained accessible.

cards.headline: New York opens AI safety registration portal, requiring disclosure from OpenAI and Anthropic
cards.teaser: Major AI developers must register by January 1 under the RAISE Act, which mandates safety frameworks and incident reporting.
cards.body:
New York opened a registration portal Tuesday for its RAISE Act, requiring large AI developers with more than $500 million in annual revenue to register by January 1, 2027. Companies including OpenAI and Anthropic must publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public transparency reports. Violations can result in fines up to $1 million for a first offense and $3 million for subsequent violations.

The newly created Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust will oversee compliance. Governor Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at SUNY Binghamton University, which will independently evaluate AI systems and review companies' safety frameworks.

cards.headline: Disney Plus app on Meta Quest adds more than 60 3D movies
cards.teaser: The updated VR app lets users stream 3D films and watch in themed virtual environments.
cards.body:
Disney has added more than 60 3D movies to the Disney Plus app on Meta Quest headsets. The updated app allows users to stream films including The Avengers and Black Panther in 3D, according to Meta.

The app also offers themed virtual environments for select films, such as a Tatooine setting for Star Wars: A New Hope and a Scare Floor environment for Monsters, Inc. Disney Plus on Meta's forthcoming VR Glasses, scheduled for spring 2027, will include IMAX Enhanced movies and additional 3D content from Lionsgate.

hero.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
hero.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
hero.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

Polish prosecutors said Monday that investigations into the suspect's motive remain ongoing, walking back earlier statements by a government minister who described the gunman as inspired by far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalism. Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, told reporters the motive inquiry continues. The suspect has not been officially named.

The attack killed four Polish citizens, a British national, and an Austrian woman in the Main Market Square. Police later found three bodies at the gunman's home, identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister. Authorities seized four firearms from the suspect's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition. Polish media reported the suspect held a firearms permit.

Sixteen people were hospitalized after the shooting, including two police officers who were injured during the gunfight with the suspect. A surgeon who was eating nearby when the attack began rushed to the scene and helped treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michał Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stem bleeding from a severely injured police officer, and that intervention undoubtedly saved the officer's life. Both wounded officers have since emerged from comas.

Poland declared two days of national mourning following the attack. Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Krakow and said the country had not previously experienced such drastic terrorism.

cards.headline: Clashes erupt in Bangladesh as supporters of ousted PM Hasina demand her return
cards.teaser: Police fired tear gas and rubber bullets as protesters demanded the return of Sheikh Hasina, who faces a death sentence and was called a fugitive by the government.
cards.body:
Police fired tear gas and rubber bullets as protesters demanded the return of Sheikh Hasina, who faces a death sentence and was called a fugitive by the government.

Police in Bangladesh fired tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina who were demanding her return from exile in India. The protests by the student wing of Hasina's banned Awami League party marked the first organized show of force by her supporters since she fled the country in August 2024 following a mass uprising.

cards.headline: Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for 69 rail crash victims
cards.teaser: King Felipe and Queen Letizia joined families and officials at a cathedral service as investigations continue into last month's deadly collision.
cards.body:
Spain's King Felipe and Queen Letizia attended a memorial service for the 69 victims of last month's high-speed rail crash near Urda, about 40 miles from Toledo. The accident occurred when one train traveling at high speed collided with a stationary train on the Madrid-Seville line. Twenty-eight people remain hospitalized.

The ceremony took place as a nationwide strike by train drivers demanding greater rail safety disrupted services across the country. Transport and Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo attended the service after taking on the transport portfolio following the resignation last week of Óscar Puente, who faced mounting pressure after the crash.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.teaser: The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.
cards.body:

The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. cards.headline: Democratic lawmakers demand answers after 8-year-old Haitian boy detained by ICE in San Diego
cards.teaser: Video shows third-grader restrained and led away by armed officers at routine check-in
cards.body:
Democratic lawmakers in California are demanding answers from the Trump administration after an eight-year-old Haitian boy was restrained and taken into federal custody by immigration officers at a check-in in San Diego on November 4. Video shows three armed officials leading the third-grader away from what his family described as a routine immigration appointment.

Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff joined four House Democrats in sending an oversight letter to homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin and health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. seeking confirmation of the child's whereabouts and steps to reunite him with family. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the boy was taken into custody because his uncle could not prove legal guardianship, and that the boy is now with the Office of Refugee Resettlement.

cards.headline: ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at routine check-in after TPS termination, prompting San Diego school district response
cards.teaser: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him
cards.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him

The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School, lost his Temporary Protected Status protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end TPS for Haitians. He was summoned to meet with ICE officers Wednesday, and his uncle brought him to the appointment to comply with the law, according to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services.

A bicycle demonstration organized to promote a boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants drew roughly 300 pro-Palestinian protesters and 200 counter-protesters to Philadelphia on Sunday,

Philadelphia police arrested a woman on an assault charge, a man on disorderly conduct, and a 17-year-old on an assault on police charge, according to a police spokesperson. Officers formed lines to keep the opposing groups separated as tensions escalated.

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney. A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

cards.headline: Oura acquires AI primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million
cards.teaser: The smart ring maker reports triple-digit revenue growth weeks after postponing its IPO.
cards.body:
Oura announced Tuesday it is acquiring Counsel Health, an AI-powered primary care platform, for $625 million. The deal comes weeks after the smart ring maker postponed its planned $2.2 billion initial public offering, citing uncertainty in the IPO market. Counsel Health, which raised $36 million in total funding, offers chat-based medical consultations and physician access through the Oura app.

Oura reported revenue of $533 million for the quarter ending September 30, up 153 percent year-over-year. The company generated $1.75 billion in revenue for fiscal year 2026, marking 92 percent annual growth. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, and the deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.

Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in

Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson announced the plan in an internal email to staff on Tuesday, saying the job cuts will begin in mid-2027. The outsourcing will start with finance, procurement, human resources, and marketing roles shifting mostly to teams in India and some to Australia.

Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude AI assistant, on Tuesday set an initial public offering price range of $70 to $78 per share, positioning what could become the largest IPO

At the midpoint, the company would raise $61 billion and achieve a valuation of roughly $1.1 trillion when combined with options and unvested stock. At the top of the range, Anthropic could be valued at $1.4 trillion.

cards.headline: President Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after board launches investigation into Chinese intelligence targeting
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump publicly defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Sunday, calling him an honorable guy and saying he would bring him on an upcoming Asia trip, hours after the company's board announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence.
cards.body:
Nvidia's board of directors announced Sunday that it is opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and hours later President Donald Trump publicly defended Huang, calling him an honorable guy who has done an amazing job for the country.

Trump said he would support bringing Huang on his upcoming trip through Asia and when asked by reporters if he wished he had acted on intelligence about Alice Huang, the president said no. The investigation comes after The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman the newspapers said had been recruited to spy for China.

Counsel Health uses AI to generate responses based on wearable health data and connects users to its network of about 50 physicians. Oura plans to link wearables, clinical AI, and doctor access to support preventative care, acute episodic concerns, and specialty and chronic conditions including reproductive and cardiometabolic health. Counsel Health's 70 employees will join Oura, and the startup will continue offering its platform to other enterprise partners.

cards.headline: Anthropic's seven co-founders will each sell $250 million in shares at IPO while retaining voting control
cards.teaser: Each founder plans to sell identical stakes as the AI company pursues a public offering that could value it at $1.4 trillion.
cards.body:
Anthropic's seven co-founders will each sell 3,378,378 shares in the company's initial public offering, according to an S-1 filing. At the midpoint of the proposed $70 to $78 price range, each founder would receive approximately $250 million. The founders are CEO Dario Amodei, President Daniela Amodei, Chief Compute Officer Tom Brown, Head of Public Benefit Jack Clark, Chief Science Officer Jared Kaplan, Chief Architect Sam McCandlish, and Interpretability Research Lead Christopher Olah.

After the sale, each founder will hold roughly 3.2% of Class A shares and one share of Class F stock with supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of voting power while owning about 22% of Class A shares. The group left OpenAI in 2021 to start Anthropic.

cards.headline: OpenAI acquires AI travel startup Odessia in apparent acqui-hire
cards.teaser: The company hired Sonder founder Francis Davidson, who built the year-old startup, but has not announced travel-specific products.
cards.body:
OpenAI acquired Odessia, an AI travel agent startup founded by Francis Davidson, who announced he now works for OpenAI helping with the future of travel. Terms were not disclosed, and the acquisition appears to be an acqui-hire. The year-old Odessia raised six million dollars in pre-seed funding led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent about five months ago before shutting down.

OpenAI confirmed the hire but has not announced new travel products, though ChatGPT users frequently ask about travel planning. Davidson previously founded Sonder, a short-term apartment rental company that reached unicorn status before filing for bankruptcy in 2025 after a key Marriott partnership ended. OpenAI counts Booking.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners.

Disney has added more than 60 3D movies to the Disney Plus app on Meta Quest headsets. The updated app allows users to stream films including The Avengers and Black Panther in 3D, according to Meta.

The app also offers themed virtual environments for select films, such as a Tatooine setting for Star Wars: A New Hope and a Scare Floor environment for Monsters, Inc. Disney Plus on Meta's forthcoming VR Glasses, scheduled for spring 2027, will include IMAX Enhanced movies and additional 3D content from Lionsgate.

hero.headline: Vikings acquire Kirk Cousins from Raiders in trade deadline deal
hero.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick, Yahoo Sports confirmed Tuesday. The trade reunites Cousins with the franchise where he last started in 2023 and addresses Minnesota's struggling quarterback situation following Carson Wentz's three-turnover, 81-yard performance in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo.

Cousins, 38, has completed his best season in years with the Raiders, throwing 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions through nine games. His performance helped Las Vegas rank eighth in points per game this season after finishing last in that category in 2025. Only Cincinnati's Joe Burrow has thrown more touchdown passes this season.

The Raiders, sitting at 4-5 and still in playoff contention, had previously signaled interest in keeping Cousins. The presence of 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, a quarterback from Indiana who has yet to start, ultimately led Las Vegas to change course and trade the veteran. The move signals the Raiders are ready to begin the Mendoza era.

For Minnesota, the acquisition represents an upgrade over the team's current options. Kyler Murray has failed to establish himself as the answer through six starts, and Wentz's Monday night collapse made clear the Vikings needed a change. With an elite defense already in place, the team views Cousins as the missing piece for a Super Bowl run. It remains unclear whether Cousins will start Sunday when Minnesota visits Green Bay at Lambeau Field, the same opponent and venue where he last started for the Vikings in Week 8 of 2023. The trade is pending Cousins passing a physical.

cards.headline: Chiefs acquire Colts WR Josh Downs in trade deadline deal
cards.teaser: Kansas City adds receiving depth to bolster passing attack that has become increasingly one-dimensional.
cards.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks, according to ESPN. The trade gives quarterback Patrick Mahomes another target alongside Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and tight end Travis Kelce as Kansas City addresses a passing offense where wide receivers have accounted for just 46 percent of receiving yards through Week 9, second-lowest in the NFL.

Downs is the second Colts receiver traded ahead of the deadline, following Keenan Allen's move to San Francisco, as Indianapolis committed to a rebuild after a two-win start. The Colts traded four players on expiring contracts to accumulate draft capital for roster reconstruction under a new general manager yet to be hired.

cards.headline: Broncos acquire Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley in division trade
cards.teaser: Denver sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder to Los Angeles for the versatile linebacker, bolstering depth behind starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad.
cards.body:
The Denver Broncos acquired linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, sending a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder to their division rival. The move addresses depth at a position where Denver has relied heavily on starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, who have logged high snap counts while younger backups remain largely untested on defense.

Henley, 26, has started 41 of 42 games over the past three seasons and posted 51 tackles, one interception, and two tackles for loss this year. The former third-round pick is in the final year of his rookie contract and is known for coverage skills after converting from safety. Denver sits atop the AFC West at 7-2 after winning five straight games.

cards.headline: Bills acquire safety Amani Hooker from Titans in trade deadline deal
cards.teaser: Buffalo addressed a defensive need by trading for the Tennessee starter, sending a second-round pick in the deal.
cards.body:
The Buffalo Bills traded for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, addressing a need at the position. Buffalo sent a second-round pick to Tennessee in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-round pick.

Hooker, a fourth-round pick in 2019, started 74 games for the Titans and became the starting strong safety in 2021. The 28-year-old has five interceptions this season and is under contract through 2028. His base salary for the remainder of the season is approximately $2 million.

cards.headline: Colts reject multiple trade offers for running back Jonathan Taylor
cards.teaser: Indianapolis declined second-round picks and additional compensation from several teams ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
cards.body:
The Indianapolis Colts will not trade running back Jonathan Taylor before Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline, despite receiving multiple offers that included second-round picks and additional compensation. The Colts wanted a blockbuster offer to even consider dealing Taylor, according to reports.

The decision comes as Indianapolis made several moves aimed at the future, including trading receiver Keenan Allen to San Francisco earlier Tuesday. The Colts also informed quarterback Daniel Jones he would not be traded before the deadline.

cards.headline: Steelers scale back pursuit of trade deadline wide receiver, insider says
cards.teaser: Pittsburgh has shifted approach on acquiring pass catchers as Tuesday's deadline nears.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have pulled back from aggressively pursuing a wide receiver trade ahead of the NFL trade deadline Tuesday, according to NFL Network insider James Palmer. Palmer said the team has pivoted from its earlier stance, though it continues to monitor the market.

The shift aligns with reports that Pittsburgh is unwilling to spend significant draft capital before the deadline. Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs has been most frequently linked to the Steelers, though the team's recent track record acquiring receivers via trade has been mixed. Head coach Mike McCarthy indicated injured receiver Michael Pittman Jr. could return soon.

cards.headline: NFL reinstates Brandon Aiyuk, agent expects him to play this season with new team
cards.teaser: The receiver has been reinstated by the league, with the 49ers holding a two-game roster exemption.
cards.body:
The NFL has reinstated wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, and the San Francisco 49ers have a two-game roster exemption for him. Agent Drew Rosenhaus said he expects Aiyuk to play this season, likely with a team that knows him, suggesting a move away from San Francisco.

Reports indicated Aiyuk was likely to be released. Rosenhaus has been working to help Aiyuk revive his career after the reinstatement.

hero.headline: David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct, including grooming allegations involving 15-year-old, after losing court bid
hero.body:
David Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women, including allegations of grooming involving a 15-year-old, after the British entertainer lost a legal bid to block publication of the claims. The Guardian and ITV News published the allegations Tuesday following a three-year joint investigation. Walliams's agent has dropped him, and the BBC removed his sketch comedy series Little Britain from its streaming service.

The allegations include claims from two women who say they first met Walliams when they were 15. One woman alleged she met him at a fan event in 2004 and that they later had sex when she was 17, which she now characterizes as grooming. Another woman alleged she met Walliams at a café in 2007 when she was 15, and that he later kissed her, lifted her shirt, and committed what she now describes as a sexual assault. Additional women accused Walliams of inappropriate behavior at Britain's Got Talent, including invitations to his dressing room, and alleged he pursued relationships with junior employees at publisher HarperCollins.

In a letter to journalists, Walliams said he is not a sexual predator and has not broken the law. He acknowledged behaving thoughtlessly in casual sexual relationships and said he regretted not taking people's feelings into account. He denied grooming or sexually harassing anyone and said he is devastated that some women he met 10 to 20 years ago have expressed hurt or anger. Walliams denied having sexual contact with the woman who alleged assault at age 15 and said he believed another woman was 18 when they had sex.

Walliams, 55, had brought legal action against ITV News and the Guardian to prevent publication, with his lawyers arguing it would be highly likely to lead him to kill himself. A High Court judge rejected the injunction request last week. Following publication, HarperCollins announced it was dropping Walliams as an author and would no longer publish his backlist. Sky also said it was dropping an upcoming adaptation of one of his books and removing his content from its platforms. The Metropolitan Police said it has contacted the news organizations to ensure potential victims are aware of how to report criminal allegations.

cards.headline: Donnie Dunagan, voice of Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
cards.teaser: Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.
cards.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.

Dunagan's brief acting career spanned just seven films over a few years but included two enduring roles. At age four, he made his film debut in 1938's Mother Carey's Chickens.

cards.headline: M. John Harrison becomes oldest Booker Prize winner at 81 for post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything
cards.teaser: M. John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, receiving the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything. Harrison, 81,
cards.body:
M. John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, receiving the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything. Harrison, 81,

Harrison, 81, was named the winner of the £50,000 prize at a ceremony in London on Monday, surpassing Margaret Atwood as the oldest recipient in the award's history. The End of Everything is set in the years after a mysterious catastrophe that caused British society to collapse.

cards.headline: Denis Villeneuve says he is finishing Dune: Part Three while beginning James Bond movie, teases casting before joking at LACMA gala
cards.teaser: Director Denis Villeneuve said Saturday that he is putting final touches on the 70mm Imax print of Dune: Part Three while simultaneously starting work on his James Bond film. Speak
cards.body:
Director Denis Villeneuve said Saturday that he is putting final touches on the 70mm Imax print of Dune: Part Three while simultaneously starting work on his James Bond film. Speak

Speaking at the LACMA Art and Film Gala in Los Angeles, where he was honored, Villeneuve called the third Dune installment a very personal project and the completion of 10 years of work in the desert. Villeneuve declined to comment on Bond casting speculation on the red carpet, saying every word would be scrutinized, but added that he is having a great time.

cards.headline: Russell Brand sentencing hearing underway after rape and sexual assault convictions
cards.teaser: A sentencing hearing for Russell Brand is underway at Southwark Crown Court in London, where prosecutors are seeking a 10 to 15 year prison term for rape and sexual assault convict
cards.body:
A sentencing hearing for Russell Brand is underway at Southwark Crown Court in London, where prosecutors are seeking a 10 to 15 year prison term for rape and sexual assault convict

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC called for a serious category one sentence, arguing Brand abused his position and degraded and humiliated his victims. Karmy-Jones told the judge that Brand held the view he could abuse without impunity and must bear responsibility for the culture around him that enabled his offending for years.

cards.headline: James Gunn and Peter Safran ousted as DC Studios co-CEOs, leaving Superman and Batman franchises in uncertainty
cards.teaser: James Gunn and Peter Safran have been removed as co-CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios after four years leading the comic book film division, throwing the future of Superman, Batman,
cards.body:
James Gunn and Peter Safran have been removed as co-CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios after four years leading the comic book film division, throwing the future of Superman, Batman,

Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham, who produced superhero films including Iron Man, The Avengers, and Spider-Man: Homecoming, will take over leadership of the studio. Gunn and Safran launched a rebooted DC Universe in 2025 with Superman, starring David Corenswet as the Man of Steel, which earned $618 million worldwide.

cards.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero heads toward $32 million opening weekend, surpassing predecessor's total domestic run
cards.teaser: Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar
cards.body:
Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar

The sequel, which centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla's return, is outpacing Godzilla Minus One, which opened in December 2023 with $11.4 million and finished its domestic run at $57.1 million. The film holds a 90 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

hero.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
hero.teaser: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou
hero.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode about a potential bid. Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January.

Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years. Democrats are scheduled to meet as a group Tuesday to discuss their path forward. Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who met with Van Hollen on Monday, said she will not vote for a majority leader candidate who cannot articulate a plan, especially for the first 100 days. Slotkin declined over the weekend to rule out her own leadership ambitions.

Both Van Hollen and Slotkin are viewed as potential presidential contenders. Van Hollen had previously suggested his focus was on 2028 and ensuring Democrats win back the White House.

Schumer needs only a majority of the Democratic caucus to win the leadership election during a closed-door meeting scheduled for early December. Many Senate Democrats have expressed support for Schumer following the party's performance in last week's midterm elections. Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said Monday he plans to continue supporting Schumer but added that the Senate needs new ideas, energy from incoming members, and changes in how it operates.

cards.headline: Seven Republican senators call for delay in GOP leadership elections
cards.teaser: Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections
cards.body:
Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections

The elections are scheduled for Tuesday, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is still expected to be reelected to lead the Senate GOP. Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's companies face Democratic investigations after $475 million midterm spending resulted in losses
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4
cards.body:
Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4

Armed with subpoena power, Democrats are preparing to examine Musk's Department of Government Efficiency operation, its access to sensitive government data, and whether his companies benefited from his influence over the Trump administration. More than 99 percent of Musk's traceable spending went to losing candidates, according to WIRED.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C

Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation. Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.

cards.headline: Attorney General dismisses Calley Means' White House corruption allegations as former FDA chief backs some claims
cards.teaser: Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg
cards.body:
Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg

Blanche told CNN he would not investigate claims Means made on a podcast, even as former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary corroborated aspects of the allegations and Representative Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican, said any impropriety claims should be examined. Means alleged in a Friday interview that former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles blocked an initiative to examine children's sugar consumption because she wanted sugar industry donations for midterm elections.
